name: United Arab Emirates
tagline: Four admissions systems, one flag — and the Gulf’s most generous financial aid
summary: The UAE imports its universities. Dubai's academic free zones host British, Australian, Indian and American campuses awarding their home degrees; Abu Dhabi hosts NYU and the Sorbonne; and alongside them sit two federal universities built for Emirati nationals and a handful of UAE-owned private institutions awarding their own. Teaching is in English almost everywhere and the IB is read as a matter of routine. What is not routine is the calendar, because there is no calendar — there is no national admissions authority, no central portal and no shared deadline, and the four kinds of institution admit on four different timetables months apart. NYU Abu Dhabi closes on 1 November for the following autumn and decides on predicted grades. RIT Dubai will take an application on 22 August. Heriot-Watt Dubai will take one three weeks before term starts. Knowing which of those four you are dealing with is the whole skill of applying here.
whyConsider: NYU Abu Dhabi meets demonstrated financial need for admitted students regardless of nationality, and all its aid for non-Emirati citizens is need-based. Against a 2026-27 cost of attendance of USD 90,434, that is the difference between an impossible option and a free one.

A branch campus awards the home institution's degree — a Heriot-Watt, Birmingham, Wollongong or Middlesex degree, recognised in Europe, obtained in the Gulf — and Birmingham Dubai states that it applies the same entry requirements as its UK campus.

An application to a UK university's Dubai campus does not go through UCAS and does not use one of your five UCAS choices. Birmingham Dubai charges nothing for it either. It costs a student almost nothing to hold alongside a UK application.
Several institutions here still accept applications after IB results are released on 6 July, which is unusual anywhere and rare in Europe.
Everything is taught in English and the IB is a standard entry qualification throughout.
No income tax, a large and young international population, and flight connections to everywhere — Copenhagen is around seven hours.
watchOuts: Treating the UAE as one deadline is the mistake this page exists to prevent. Its institutions are eight months apart: NYU Abu Dhabi's Early Decision I closes 1 November 2026 for a 2027 start, and RIT Dubai's Fall 2027 deadline is 22 August 2027. Nine of the fourteen institutions here have published no 2027 date at all, and the record says for each one whether that is because the university said the date is coming or because it published nothing.

A branch campus is not the parent university with better weather. It is licensed separately — nationally by the Commission for Academic Accreditation under MoHESR, and in Dubai by KHDA, in Abu Dhabi by ADEK — and teaches a subset of the parent's programmes with its own staff. What it does share is the degree, and sometimes the entry requirements. Check both rather than assuming either.

Every foreign school certificate needs attestation by the local education authority and then an equivalency certificate from the UAE Ministry of Education. Khalifa University states that applications with missing documents will not be accepted. This is slow and it is not optional.

The federal universities are not really open to you. UAEU and Zayed University direct places and subsidies at UAE nationals and children of Emirati mothers, who apply through a national placement route, and run international admission as a separate and much smaller stream. Establish eligibility before investing effort.
NYU Abu Dhabi's Early Decision rounds are binding. You are released from the agreement only if the financial aid package will not let you attend — not because a better offer arrives.
Only two UAE tuition figures were established in this research, NYU Abu Dhabi's and Khalifa's. Everything else is blank on purpose and has to be read off the university's own fee page.

The UAE is socially conservative by Danish standards. Laws on alcohol, relationships outside marriage and public behaviour differ from what you are used to, and enforcement varies by emirate. Read the Danish foreign ministry's travel advice properly, not the marketing brochures.
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Check su.dk before budgeting.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: There is no national minimum, because there is no national rule-owner for admission. Two institutions publish one: Khalifa University requires the full Diploma with a minimum of 4 in each of six HL/SL subjects and 24 points in total, and RIT Dubai requires 28 points for engineering and 24 for computing, business, psychology and new media design. Neither figure may be read across to any other institution, and the other twelve are not established.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Set per institution. Khalifa University requires Mathematics as a mandatory subject plus one science — Physics, Biology or Chemistry depending on the programme — and excludes Islamic Education from the six subjects it counts. RIT Dubai requires Mathematics, Physics and one of Chemistry or Biology at grade 4 or above for engineering. Branch campuses apply the parent university's subject rules, so the page to read is the parent's.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No conversion table exists and none is needed: UAE institutions read IB points directly. What they do require, and what no European system asks for, is a UAE Ministry of Education equivalency certificate for the Diploma, on top of attestation of the transcript by the local education authority — KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi, SPEA in Sharjah.
notes: The UAE has one of the largest concentrations of IB World Schools in the region, so admissions offices read the transcript fluently. That fluency is about reading it, not about publishing what they want from it.

Khalifa University grants advanced standing credit for a score of 6 or higher on certain HL subjects, which can shorten the degree. It gives no credit for lower scores, and where an exam is sat twice the higher score counts.
RIT Dubai publishes how it reads an IB English grade rather than demanding a test: 7 and 4–6 both reach its highest writing course, 3 the one below. That is rare and worth having.
Minimum IB scores are not established for the other twelve institutions in this record. That is a gap in the research, not evidence that they have none.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Effectively all of them outside Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi. English is the medium of instruction across the private sector, the branch campuses, NYU Abu Dhabi, Khalifa and the American University of Sharjah.
language.englishProof: Set per institution and not waived by the IB as a matter of course. RIT Dubai requires IELTS 6.5 for full admission and will take 5.0–6.0 conditionally, while exempting students from English-medium curricula including the IB and placing them by their English subject grade. Birmingham Dubai lists an English proficiency test among its required documents. Check each one; do not assume an IB in English clears it.
notes: Arabic is the official language and English is the working language of the country. In Dubai you can live for years without needing Arabic.

Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi is the real exception. Most of its bachelors are taught in French and entry to those requires a B2-level French certificate — DELF, TEF, TCF or its own SELFEE — rather than an IB French grade. That is a named external qualification and it takes time to obtain.
Federal institutions teach some programmes in Arabic. Check the medium of instruction programme by programme.

feeContext.summary: The UAE does not recognise EU or EEA status and gives it no advantage. The categories that exist are UAE national, resident and international, and a Danish student is in the last. See the non-EU row.

Two figures were established and the rest were not. NYU Abu Dhabi's 2026-27 cost of attendance is USD 90,434, of which tuition is USD 68,574 — before need-based aid, which most admitted non-Emiratis receive. Khalifa University charges AED 2,500 per credit hour, which its own page puts at roughly AED 81,250 a year at 12–16 credits, with campus housing at AED 10,000–20,000 per semester. No other UAE institution's fee could be read from its own pages in this research, and nothing here should be assumed to apply to another institution.

sectorLandscape.summary: The UAE's higher education divides by who owns and licenses the institution, not by where it is. Three kinds dominate and they behave completely differently: federal institutions built for Emirati nationals, UAE-owned private universities awarding their own degrees, and branch campuses of foreign universities awarding the parent's. Behind all three sits a licensing layer rather than an admissions one — the Commission for Academic Accreditation licenses nationally under MoHESR, KHDA licenses and certifies degrees in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi — and the free zones such as Dubai International Academic City and Dubai Knowledge Park are where the branch campuses physically sit. There is no national admissions authority at all, which is why this Destination has four routes and no portal.

routes.what: United Arab Emirates University in Al Ain and Zayed University in Abu Dhabi and Dubai. Government-owned, heavily subsidised, and built to educate Emirati nationals — places and money go to nationals and children of Emirati mothers first, who apply through a national placement route a foreign applicant cannot use. International admission exists as a separate and much smaller stream that you contact the university about directly.
routes.note: Neither publishes an undergraduate deadline for 2027. Zayed says its dates are to be confirmed; UAEU says applications happen during announced periods and announces none.

routes.what: The institution type nobody mentions to foreigners, and the largest higher education institution in the country: a federal network of seven colleges across Abu Dhabi, Al Ain, Al Dhafra, Dubai, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah and Sharjah, awarding applied diplomas and bachelor's degrees across around forty programmes. It is the UAE's nearest equivalent to a Danish erhvervsakademi — shorter, vocational, employer-facing — and it is invisible in every English-language guide to studying in the Gulf.
routes.note: HCT runs an international student portal, so it is not closed to foreign applicants. What the IB buys you there, and what it costs, are not established here. Recorded because it exists and because a student who would suit it will not otherwise hear of it.

routes.what: UAE-owned, fee-paying institutions licensed by the Commission for Academic Accreditation and awarding their own degrees — Khalifa University, the American University of Sharjah, the American University in Dubai, Canadian University Dubai. Several are American or Canadian in structure and accreditation without being anyone's branch campus, which is a distinction worth holding onto: the degree is theirs, not an imported one.
routes.note: These are the institutions whose 2027 dates are least likely to be published yet and the ones to re-check from autumn 2026. Khalifa is the country's strongest research university and admits by competitive test; the others are more accessible.

routes.englishName: branch campus of a foreign university
routes.what: A foreign university operating a campus in a UAE free zone and awarding its home degree: Heriot-Watt Dubai, University of Birmingham Dubai, Middlesex Dubai, the University of Wollongong in Dubai, RIT Dubai, SP Jain Dubai, Sorbonne University Abu Dhabi. The degree, and often the entry requirements, come from the parent — Birmingham Dubai states it applies the same entry requirements as its UK campus, and Heriot-Watt lets students move between its Dubai, Edinburgh and Malaysia campuses mid-degree. The dates, the fees and the visa come from the UAE campus.
routes.note: You apply directly to the campus, not through UCAS, and a Dubai application does not use one of your five UCAS choices. Most of these publish no deadline at all; Heriot-Watt Dubai publishes a policy instead, saying it admits on a rolling basis up to three weeks before term.

routes.what: Institutions owned by or built around a single national employer or sector — aviation, hospitality, security, energy — training directly into it. They sit outside the university listings and outside most guidance, and they are a real route for a student who already knows the industry they want.
routes.note: Named because the route exists and is otherwise invisible, not because it has been researched. No institution of this kind is recorded in this Destination yet and nothing about entry, cost or IB access is established.

jurisdictions.name: NYU Abu Dhabi — admitted through NYU
jurisdictions.summary: One institution, and its own jurisdiction because nothing else in the UAE works like it. NYU Abu Dhabi is one of NYU's three degree-granting campuses and admits through the Common Application on the American calendar, with two binding Early Decision rounds and a Regular Decision that closes on 5 January — six months before IB results. Grouping it with the other branch campuses would put a November deadline and an August one in the same box.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: 1 November, 1 January and 5 January, all 23:59 EST, with decisions on 15 December, 15 February and 1 April. The two Early Decision rounds are binding. Every year here is inferred from a bare recurring date and is provisional.

variations.label: Cost and aid
variations.summary: 2026-27 cost of attendance USD 90,434, of which tuition is USD 68,574. All financial aid grants to non-Emirati citizens are need-based and the university meets demonstrated need, so very few international students pay the sticker price. The CSS Profile is a separate application with its own deadline.

jurisdictions.name: Branch campuses admitting on their own calendar
jurisdictions.summary: Foreign universities' UAE campuses that run their own admissions: Heriot-Watt Dubai, Birmingham Dubai, Middlesex Dubai, the University of Wollongong in Dubai, RIT Dubai, SP Jain Dubai and Sorbonne Abu Dhabi. The degree and usually the entry requirements come from the parent; the dates, the fees and the visa come from the campus. You apply directly and not through UCAS.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: Only RIT Dubai publishes dates: Early phase 15 January, Regular 31 May, deadline 22 August, with late applications reviewed on space availability. Heriot-Watt Dubai publishes a policy instead — rolling, up to three weeks before term. Birmingham Dubai, Middlesex Dubai, UOWD and SP Jain Dubai publish no application deadline at all. Sorbonne Abu Dhabi has published 2026 and not 2027.

variations.label: Visas
variations.summary: Birmingham Dubai sets a separate, harder deadline for new international students to apply for a University-sponsored visa from outside the UAE — 24 August 2026 for the September 2026 intake. For an applicant living in Denmark this, not the application, is the binding date, and the 2027 one is not yet published.

jurisdictions.name: UAE private universities
jurisdictions.summary: UAE-owned institutions licensed by the Commission for Academic Accreditation and awarding their own degrees: Khalifa University, the American University of Sharjah, the American University in Dubai and Canadian University Dubai. Each admits directly on its own calendar, and no two of those calendars agree.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: AUS opens Fall 2027 on 19 October 2026 and sets Early File Completion on 5 July 2027 — the day before IB results — but publishes no closing date for Fall. Khalifa says its Fall 2027 timeline is still to come. Canadian University Dubai publishes one academic year at a time and sets international deadlines about a week ahead of domestic ones. The American University in Dubai publishes month ranges rather than dates.

variations.label: Cost
variations.summary: Khalifa University publishes AED 2,500 per credit hour, which it puts at roughly AED 81,250 a year at 12–16 credits, plus AED 10,000–20,000 per semester for campus housing, and includes any scholarship in the admission offer rather than in a separate application. No fee was established for the other three.

jurisdictions.name: Federal institutions
jurisdictions.summary: United Arab Emirates University and Zayed University. Government-owned and built for Emirati nationals, who reach them through a national placement route a foreign applicant cannot use. International admission is a separate, smaller stream handled directly by the university, and neither institution publishes an undergraduate deadline for 2027.

variations.label: Deadlines
variations.summary: Zayed University's undergraduate application page says "Application Dates to be confirmed". UAEU says applicants apply through the ministry's portal during announced application periods and publishes no undergraduate period — although it does publish graduate ones.

variations.label: Cost
variations.summary: Not established. Whether an international student pays a different fee from a subsidised Emirati one, and whether the international stream is capped, were both looked for and neither is published.

notes: Grouping decision. institutionGrouping is "jurisdiction" with four jurisdictions each of kind "sector", rather than the "sector" grouping. The distinction is not cosmetic: what divides UAE institutions is not where they are but who licenses them and whose calendar they admit on, and each of those divisions has its own Application Route, its own dates and its own cost story — which is what an Application Jurisdiction is for and what the sector grouping, which carries no route, is not. Grouping by emirate would have put Birmingham Dubai next to Middlesex Dubai and away from Birmingham UK, which is the wrong way round.

NYU Abu Dhabi is a branch campus and is still its own jurisdiction. It admits through NYU's system on the American calendar, with a binding Early Decision closing 1 November — eight months before anything else recorded here. Leaving it in the branch-campus group would have rebuilt exactly the lump this pass was opened to dissolve.

Every NYU Abu Dhabi and RIT Dubai date is provisional. Both publish bare recurring days with no year, so the 2027 years are inferred. NYUAD's Early Decision I falls on 1 November 2026 on that inference, five weeks after this record was written, and needs confirming before anyone acts on it.

Not established: tuition for twelve of the fourteen institutions; minimum IB points for twelve of the fourteen; whether NYU Abu Dhabi is need-blind for international applicants; whether the federal universities charge international students differently or cap the international stream; whether any branch campus runs a different process for an applicant living outside the UAE beyond the visa step; work rights on a student residence visa, which are not re-verified from an official source here.
Programme-level records not yet created. Stages 1–5 of the research brief are done for this Destination; stage 6 is not.
